{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABbLCCXA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhEwVnw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 168, "title": "Add genuine local streaming TTS with Qwen3-TTS and CosyVoice3 candidates", "body": "## Goal

Add **genuine local streaming TTS** to the Chrome extension, based on **Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice** and **CosyVoice3 0.5B**. The intended experience is: as TTS generates audio, its first audio chunks begin playing through Speaker **before the utterance is fully synthesized**. This is **not** just faster full-clip generation, chunking a finished WAV, or queuing completed `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO` clips.

Target models:
- [Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS) ([weights/card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice)): Japanese/English, model-native streaming.
- [Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512](https://huggingface.co/FunAudioLLM/Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512) ([CosyVoice upstream](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice)): text-in/audio-out bi-streaming architecture.

**Important:** upstream Python/CUDA streaming support is **not evidence** that the model runs in a Chrome MV3 Worker / WebGPU / WASM with true incremental decoding. Validate the actual model assets, runtime, tokenizer/vocoder, licenses, memory and browser compatibility before exposing a Node. Do not claim either model is supported without real local browser inference. Keep any unsupported candidate's status and blockers explicit; do not silently mark its implementation complete.

## Current limitation

- `Supertonic3` and `Kokoro` Worker RPCs each return a full waveform per `generate` call.
- The current `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO` contract represents a **completed** mono PCM clip.
- `SpeakerOutput` plays completed clips sequentially but cannot start a clip before its TTS Node has emitted a completed waveform.

## Intended graph

```text
ASR.final / committed translation text
    → Qwen3-TTS Streaming (or CosyVoice3 Streaming)
    → incremental audio chunks
    → Speaker (continuous ordered playback)
```

Use a clearly discoverable streaming TTS Node / mode in the **existing** Graph Editor. Keep today's nonstreaming Supertonic3, Kokoro and manual Audio player / WAV paths unchanged. Prefer the smallest explicit port contract needed for audio chunks rather than teaching generic sinks to guess whether a completed `SYNTHESIZED_AUDIO` value is a segment. Do not invent a framework or device manager.

## Implementation requirements

1. **Real model-specific browser execution:** investigate both upstream candidates and implement genuinely incremental generation for each viable candidate in an extension-owned local Worker. Use an immutable, reviewed model/runtime/asset set, explicit Save/Models preparation, cache-only Start, and existing MV3 CSP rules. No online inference service, Python server dependency, silent CPU/cloud fallback or recording-time weight downloads.
2. **Incremental audio delivery:** emit usable sequential PCM chunks as they are generated, with sufficient stream boundaries/order/sample-rate metadata to prevent cross-utterance mixing, reorder or accidental replay. First audible playback must start *before full synthesis completes*. Make end-of-utterance and error/abort semantics explicit. Maintain producer-independent typed ports.
3. **Speaker playback:** extend the existing Speaker path minimally (or use a distinct explicitly typed streaming input where needed) to schedule successive chunks without overlaps, substantial artificial gaps, or runaway buffering. Handle audio context activation from Start, rate mismatch/conversion, backpressure/queue limits, Stop-drain, Cancel-immediate-stop, and teardown. Preserve existing completed-clip playback behavior.
4. **Text input semantics:** start with committed `TEXT` inputs and ordered utterances; if a candidate genuinely supports incremental text input, expose that capability explicitly without interpreting revisable ASR provisional text as immutable speech. No duplicate spoken phrases after revisions or reconnects.
5. **Resource limits and UI:** show model readiness and actionable errors through the existing UI; avoid additional global modes or permanent panels. Document minimum hardware and memory realistically. Make model selection explicit via Node type or a small existing-style setting; no hidden switching between models.
6. **Evidence:** for Qwen3-TTS and CosyVoice3 separately, document what works on the targeted local browser runtime. If either candidate is infeasible with available browser-compatible weights/runtime, record the concrete blocker and keep its unsupported capability clearly tracked; seek an explicit scope adjustment or separate follow-up rather than claiming that both have shipped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A saved graph produces **Japanese and English** speech via at least the proven model path, with real local TTS and audio starting before the corresponding utterance finishes generating. Verify with timestamped chunk and playback evidence—not a mock-only demo.
- [ ] Both named model candidates have separate, evidence-backed browser/MV3 feasibility conclusions. Any supported model has a working streaming path; any unsupported model is not advertised as runnable.
- [ ] Consecutive utterances and chunks preserve ordering and boundaries, with no repetition, overlap or unbounded queues; Stop drains accepted audio, Cancel terminates playback/generation, and late Worker replies cannot restart audio.
- [ ] Explicit Graph Editor ports, Save/reload, validation, model asset preparation, CSP, diagnostics and existing TTS/AudioOutput/complete-clip Speaker behavior are covered; no unexpected migration for old saved graphs.
- [ ] Tests include browser/MV3 real incremental playback checks where models are available, plus deterministic boundary/queue/abort tests. Report hardware/model-asset limitations honestly.
- [ ] No new server/cloud dependency, speculative abstraction, or 'streaming' label on a full-clip-only implementation.

## Context

- `web/tts-nodes.js`, `web/tts-worker.js`, `web/synthesized-audio.js`, `web/speaker-output.js`
- `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/tts-cache.js`, `docs/tts-nodes.md`
- #164 (Speaker automatic sequential playback, implemented)
- Design principles: single-responsibility Nodes, explicit typed ports, local-first execution, Keep it simple.

## Required post-merge verification

For any shipped streaming model, verify first-audio-before-generation-complete using real pinned assets in a packaged extension on documented hardware; record first-chunk and playback timestamps. If this is not executable in the implementation environment, do not claim the streaming model is production-verified.
